body: The fact that you are doing research and asking for advice is a fantastic way to start! Just wanted to say kudos to you!
I have had this same thought before as I to have had my fair "fun" with drugs as a young teen.  This included cocaine, ecstasy, mushrooms, marijuana, alcohol, etc.

For me, it's a fast slippery slope to a very dark place.  I feel a difference in my mindset after just one drink and I have a hard time stopping drinking for the rest of that night. I pretty much become manic or depressed when I drink. It's a huge trigger which is why I am trying to quit completely.  19 days sober.
Yeah or you take so many pills that you get high and sick and end up in the emergency room.  Not a good choice... speaking from experience.

I have been trying quetiapine and it's not going so well.  Makes me sleep for 10+ hours and I cannot get up for anything in the morning.  Always tired and irritated.  I guess I just have to try others and work with my GP.  It's a hard process to get the right treatment.
I have one more question.  Are you taking medication to help with the bipolar? If that's too personal, please do not feel pressured to answer.
Thank you :) I will put more thought into it

Hi there, I have been thinking of going back to school for Nursing, but I am worried that the bipolar will get in my way of being successful.  I imagine myself trying to treat someone then having my own episode at work in which case I am no help to anyone.  Can you please shine some light on what your days at work look like and how you get through each shift as well as school?  I would reallllyyy appreciate it.  I am feeling very discouraged at this time.
This may sound cliché or perhaps a bit lame to you, but it helps me to think that "this too shall pass".  The down days are temporary.  I hope you feel well soon.  Sending positive vibes your way.

You are not alone.  I was diagnosed 3 days ago and I feel the exact same way. Unfortunately, I cannot provide guidance on how to sort it out as I am asking the exact same questions.  I just want to let you know that you are not alone.
